messages.subject: Nimble multiple contraint problems
parts:
Hello, I am trying to add some contraints in my nimble code:

constraint_data1[j] ~ dconstraint(xLambda12[j] + xLambda1[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda12[j] + xLambda2[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda13[j] + xLambda1[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda13[j] + xLambda3[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda23[j] + xLambda2[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda23[j] + xLambda3[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda123[j] + xLambda1[j] + xLambda13[j] + xLambda12[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda123[j] + xLambda2[j] + xLambda23[j] + xLambda12[j] > 0 &
                                  xLambda123[j] + xLambda3[j] + xLambda13[j] + xLambda23[j] > 0)

Unfortunately, it did not work as my expectation. Some constraints did not work.
For example, in some samples, the contraint in j =14 did not work.  
Since my contraint code in j =14 is:
xLambda123[14] + xLambda2[14] + xLambda23[14] + xLambda12[14] > 0
I expect that every sample should follow this contraint, but some of the the results show that  (Lambda123[14] + Lambda2[14] + Lambda23[14] + Lambda12[14]) are smaller than 0. This is only a example, there are lots other similar problems in other js .
Is there any problem in my coding? Looking forward to your response!

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Nimble multiple contraint problems
parts:
Hi Hsin,

Did you make sure to add `constraint_data1` via the `data` argument to `nimbleModel`, with the values of `constraint_data1` set to 1?

(`dconstraint` is a "trick" in that it is a likelihood term that gives a probability of 1 if satisfied and 0 if not, so proposals that don't satisfy the constraint should be rejected.)

-Chris
